task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's REQ-039 test spec + test code (branch feature/WF02-REQ039-20260817). TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff (handoffs/WF02-REQ039-20260817/step-03-test-designer.json) reports an ad hoc run during drafting surfaced 2 orphan Postgres schemas from unrelated pre-existing debris, manually dropped, not reproduced across 5 subsequent clean runs -- independently sanity-check this isn't masking a real cleanup gap in the new test files themselves, don't just accept the explanation.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-039's 6 acceptance criteria has at least one runnable test targeting it (AC6 is documentation-content, verify the spec's stated direct-inspection approach is legitimate per REQ-022/REQ-020 precedent, not a skipped criterion)
No TODO: implement test left in the spec
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution
Tests are self-sufficient, don't depend on other tests running first
Independently verify the claimed 5x-clean-run / zero-orphan-schema result is credible, not just trusted

result.summary: Independently validated test/specs/REQ-039.md, test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, and test/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader_test.exs against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-039 entry (verbatim 6 ACs, requirements.yaml:1867-1872) and the actual implementation (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex). All 6 ACs have runnable, non-vacuous test coverage: AC1-2 in sandbox_pool_test.exs's 'empty pool' describe (2 tests), AC2 in 'quota exhausted, blocking path' (3 tests covering both the release-driven hand-off and the real timeout path plus the max_wait_ms<=0 edge), AC3 in 'release/1,2' (2 tests), AC4-AC5 in fixture_loader_test.exs (3 + 3 tests). AC6 (moduledoc names the process-per-instance-vs-row open question) is verified by direct inspection rather than a runtime test -- checked this against the cited precedent directly: read test/specs/REQ-022.md's AC4 section and test/specs/REQ-020.md's AC5 section, both of which use the identical direct-inspection pattern with the identical stated rationale (avoiding a String.contains?(@moduledoc, ...) test that proves nothing about truth and stays green under a copy-pasted substring), both explicitly asking RELEASE-VALIDATOR to re-confirm independently. REQ-039's spec follows the same pattern faithfully (cites lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex lines 13-30, states RELEASE-VALIDATOR should re-confirm) -- this is genuine precedent, not a skipped criterion dressed up as one. No 'TODO: implement test' anywhere (grepped spec + both test files, zero matches). No @tag :skip anywhere. Fixtures are per-test-unique: fresh Ecto.UUID.generate() ids/sandbox schema names (SandboxPool's own provisioning derives schema_name from a fresh UUID every claim), System.unique_integer/1-suffixed pool names via each file's start_pool!/1 helper -- no shared hardcoded schema or row across tests. Tests are self-sufficient: each test starts its own pool and claims its own schema, no ordering dependency; confirmed via a randomized-seed run in addition to fixed-seed runs. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in either test file (grepped for password/secret/connection-string patterns, zero matches; config/test.exs's local Postgres creds are pre-existing project config, not introduced by these files). Orphan-schema investigation (the specific focus of this gate): read on_exit/1 placement in both files and confirmed the cleanup callback is registered immediately after each successful schema-creating claim/claim_schema! call -- i.e. before any subsequent assertion in the test body that could fail -- so cleanup survives a test-body failure, not just the happy path (verified this is true in every test case in both files, not just a sampled few). Independently ran `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs test/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader_test.exs` 3 times in isolation (seed 0, ExUnit's own random seed, seed 999): 13/13 passed all three times, and queried `SELECT nspname FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'sandbox_%'` directly against the real test DB (via `mix run`, psql unavailable in this environment) before any run (0 rows, confirming a clean baseline) and after each of the 3 runs (0 rows every time). This corroborates TEST-DESIGNER's reported 5-run/zero-orphan result rather than just trusting it, and is consistent with the on_exit/1 placement analysis -- no evidence of a leak in either new file's own cleanup logic; the 2 orphan schemas TEST-DESIGNER reported from one ad hoc drafting run remain most plausibly attributable to pre-existing debris as claimed, not a systematic gap.
